author: @GregSalazar

text:
I mean, it really depends on what you're planning on using it for. MOBAs and less graphically demanding games, sure which is why AMD is targeting these lower powered cards at the lower budgeted and lightweight gaming laptop market.

But triple-A titles on an ultrawide the 480 will probably about hold its own, and I wouldn't be surprised if you start to see dipping below 60 on maxed out graphics. Especially as more games are released that are more demanding for your pixels (based on wild estimates influenced by the rumours that are knocking back and forth)

I think in that sort of scenario you'd see the 470 starting to drag behind more significantly. But it all depends on what games you want to play, what level of settings you want to play them on, how good AMD are at pushing out drivers and how well game developers optimise to, e.g. make the most of async compute etc etc.
